write_up: A recruiter sees a data analytics internship, a club treasurer role and a degree in progress. The hesitation is the internship: you name the tools and teams, but not what the reporting covered or what the dashboard showed.
The member survey line is the strongest model. It names the data you worked on and the tools you used. Give the reporting and presentation that same treatment, then add what the dashboard showed.

cards.line: The internship has no employer description beyond the credit union's name and location.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter knows it was a credit union, but not how many members it served. A short description could give the internship some context.
cards.example: Great Lakes Credit Union, Ann Arbor, MI | [brief description or member count]

cards.line: - Assisted the analytics team with weekly reporting
cards.cannot_tell: 'Assisted' leaves your part of the weekly reporting open. A recruiter also can't tell what the reports covered.

cards.question: What did the reports cover, and what part of them did you handle?

cards.line: - Cleaned member survey data in Excel and SQL
cards.cannot_tell: Keep the combination of a named data source and the tools you used. It gives a recruiter something concrete to hold onto.
